metadata.title: Predicting the hypervelocity star population in Gaia

evidence.quote:
In this section we assess the performance of Gaia in measuring
the astrometric properties of the current observed sample of HVS
candidates. Brown et al. (2015) measured proper motions with the
Hubble Space Telescope (HST) for 16 extreme radial velocity can-
didates, finding that 13 of them have trajectories consistent with a
GC origin within 2σ confidence levels, and 12 of them are unbound
to the Milky Way.

notes: Notes for HVS1, HVS2, HVS3 = HE 0437-5439, HVS4, HVS5, HVS6, HVS7, HVS8, HVS9, HVS10, HVS12, HVS13, B434, B485, B711, B733: these are the labelled members of the Brown et al. (2015) sample shown in I:p14-b0. At T:p12-b3 the paper reports group-level counts—16 candidates, 13 with GC-consistent trajectories, and 12 unbound to the Milky Way—but does not identify which 12 are unbound; all labelled sample members are therefore treated as follow_up rather than candidates_found. HVS3 is explicitly equated with HE 0437-5439 at T:p12-b4 and T:p12-b5. The synthetic VESC/HILLS/MBHB populations and unnamed HVS samples are not individually identifiable stars and are omitted.

HVS1: For HVS1, the paper reports only its expected Gaia proper-motion uncertainty compared with the HST proper-motion error in Figure 18 (I:p14-b0), and states that HVS1 is one of the stars that will not have a better proper-motion determination by Gaia (T:p12-b6). It does not report right ascension, declination, distance, parallax, individual proper-motion components, radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability for HVS1, so no quantities meeting the extraction rules are available.

HVS2: HVS2 appears only in Figure 18 (I:p14-b0), where it is a labeled red point comparing HST and Gaia total proper-motion errors. The paper does not report requested astrometric, distance, radial-velocity, galactocentric-radius, rest-frame-speed, or bound/unbound-probability values specifically for HVS2. The plotted proper-motion error values are uncertainties, not proper-motion components, so they are not retained.

HVS3: HVS3 (= HE 0437-5439) is mentioned only in the context of the current HVS sample: its G magnitude and (V-I_C) color are estimated from B and V photometry (T:p12-b4, T:p12-b5), it appears in the HST-versus-Gaia proper-motion-error comparison (T:p12-b6; I:p14-b0), and it is listed among stars expected to have better Gaia DR2 proper motions (T:p13-b3). The paper does not report individual astrometric coordinates, distance, parallax, proper-motion components, radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability for HVS3, so no eligible quantities are extracted.

HVS4: HVS4 is identified only in Section 5/Fig. 18 (T:p12-b3, I:p14-b0) as one of the 16 Brown et al. (2015) HVS candidates. The figure places HVS4 at an HST total proper-motion error of about 0.53 mas/yr and a predicted Gaia total proper-motion error of about 0.17 mas/yr; these are quadrature-sum errors, not proper-motion component values. The paper does not report HVS4's coordinates, parallax, distance, individual proper-motion components, radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, Galactic-rest-frame speed, or star-specific bound/unbound probability. HVS4 is shown as a red point, indicating a trajectory consistent with a Galactic-center origin, but that classification is not one of the requested quantities.

HVS5: HVS5 appears only as a member of the Brown et al. (2015) HVS candidate sample (T:p12-b3; T:p13-b3), and its measurement is shown in Figure 18 (I:p14-b0), which plots Gaia versus HST proper-motion errors rather than proper-motion components or other requested quantities. No eligible quantity is reported for HVS5.

HVS6: HVS6 is one of the 16 current HVS candidates from Brown et al. (2015) discussed in Section 5 and shown in Fig. 18 (I:p14-b0). The only star-specific information given is the Gaia-estimated proper-motion uncertainty (about 0.29 mas/yr) compared with the HST proper-motion uncertainty (about 1.1 mas/yr). These are measurement errors on the proper motion, not values of the proper-motion components, position, distance, parallax, radial velocity, or any bound probability for HVS6; the paper does not report such quantities for this individual star. The paper's catalogues (VESC, HILLS, MBHB) are mock populations, not results for HVS6. Therefore no eligible quantity can be extracted for this target.

HVS7: The target star HVS7 is discussed only in Section 5: T:p13-b3 lists it among seven stars expected to have improved Gaia DR2 proper-motion determinations, and I:p14-b0/Figure 18 plots its HST and Gaia total proper-motion errors (approximately 1.3 and 0.13 mas/yr, respectively) as a red point consistent with a Galactic-center origin. These are proper-motion uncertainties and a trajectory classification, not reported equatorial proper-motion components or any other eligible quantity. The paper gives no individual RA, Dec, distance, parallax, radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability for HVS7; sample-level statements (e.g. 12 of 16 unbound) are not specific to this star.

HVS8: No eligible quantity values are reported specifically for HVS8. In Section 5 (T:p13-b3), HVS8 is only listed among seven candidates that will have a better proper-motion determination in Gaia DR2; no right ascension, declination, distance, parallax, proper-motion component, radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, Galactocentric-rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability is given for this star. Figure 18 (I:p14-b0) shows HVS8's HST and Gaia predicted total proper-motion errors (plotted as a quadrature sum), but these are measurement uncertainties, not proper-motion component values.

HVS9: HVS9 appears only in Figure 18 (I:p14-b0), which compares total proper-motion errors from Gaia and HST. The paper does not report HVS9's equatorial coordinates, distance, parallax, individual proper-motion components, radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability. No eligible quantity can be extracted for this target.

HVS10: HVS10 appears only in Figure 18 (I:p14-b0), which plots HST proper-motion error versus predicted Gaia proper-motion error for the Brown et al. (2015) sample. The paper does not report right ascension, declination, distance, parallax, individual proper-motion components, radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, Galactic-rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability for HVS10 individually; only sample-level statements and a proper-motion uncertainty are given, and the latter is not one of the requested quantities.

HVS12: HVS12 is only mentioned in Section 5 (p12-b4/b5/b6) and Figure 18 (I:p14-b0) as one of the 16 HVS candidates from Brown et al. (2015). The paper reports only a comparison of its predicted Gaia proper-motion uncertainty (~0.53 mas/yr, y-axis) with the HST uncertainty (~0.35 mas/yr, x-axis) in Fig. 18; it notes that HVS12 is one of three stars (HVS1, HVS12, HVS13) that will NOT have a better proper-motion determination with Gaia, and that it is not among the 7 brightest stars observable in Gaia DR2. These are measurement uncertainties, not values of ra, dec, proper motion, parallax, distance, radial velocity, or any other target quantity. No actual astrometric, kinematic, distance, or bound/unbound values for HVS12 are reported in the supplied material.

HVS13: HVS13 is discussed only in Section 5 (T:p12-b6) and Figure 18 (I:p14-b0) as part of the comparison of Gaia versus HST proper-motion uncertainties for the Brown et al. (2015) HVS candidates. The paper states that HVS1, HVS12, and HVS13 are the three stars that will NOT have a better proper-motion determination by Gaia, and HVS13 is absent from the list of 7 stars needing better PM in DR2 (T:p13-b3). Figure 18 plots, for HVS13, an HST quadrature-sum proper-motion error of about 0.35 mas/yr and a Gaia quadrature-sum error of about 0.73 mas/yr. These are uncertainties (quadrature sums), not the star's proper-motion components or any of the defined quantities (no RA, Dec, distance, parallax, individual PM components, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, rest-frame speed, or bound probability is reported for HVS13). Therefore no quantities meeting the scientific rules were extractable for this target.

B434: B434 appears only as a labeled point in Figure 18 (I:p14-b0). That figure compares the quadrature sum of the HST proper-motion errors with the predicted Gaia proper-motion error; it does not report the star's proper-motion components or any other requested quantity. Section 5 (T:p12-b3–T:p13-b3) and the Figure 18 caption do not provide individual astrometric, distance, velocity, or probability values for B434. Therefore no requested quantities can be extracted from the supplied material.

B485: B485 appears only in Section 5 as one of seven stars expected to have a better proper-motion determination already in Gaia DR2 (T:p13-b3) and as a black point, classified as a disk runaway, in Figure 18 (I:p14-b0). Figure 18 reports HST and Gaia total proper-motion errors, not proper-motion components, and the paper reports no right ascension, declination, distance, parallax, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic-rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability for B485. Thus no requested quantity is reported for this star.

B711: The target star B711 appears only twice in the paper: in Section 5 text (T:p13-b3), which lists it among seven stars (HVS3, HVS5, HVS7, HVS8, B485, B711, B733) that will have a better proper-motion determination already in Gaia DR2, and in Figure 18 (I:p14-b0), where it is plotted as a black dot (disk runaway) at approximately x ≈ 1.2 mas/yr (HST proper-motion error) and y ≈ 0.06 mas/yr (Gaia proper-motion error). The Fig. 18 axes are the quadrature sums of proper-motion uncertainties, not proper-motion components, so they cannot be recorded as proper_motion_ra/proper_motion_dec. The paper reports no individual right ascension, declination, distance, parallax, proper-motion components, radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability for B711 (its membership in the Brown et al. 2015 radial-velocity sample is noted only collectively, without numerical values). Therefore no quantity meeting the scientific rules could be extracted for this star.

B733: The target star B733 appears only as one of the Brown et al. (2015) HVS candidates in the discussion of Gaia proper-motion performance. In T:p13-b3 it is listed among the seven brightest candidates (HVS3, HVS5, HVS7, HVS8, B485, B711, B733) that will have a better proper-motion determination already in Gaia DR2, and it is plotted as a labelled point in I:p14-b0 (Fig. 18), which compares HST and Gaia proper-motion errors. The paper does not report numerical values for B733's right ascension, declination, distance, parallax, proper-motion components, radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, Galactic-rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability. Fig. 18 gives only a graphical comparison of the quadrature-summed proper-motion error, not the proper-motion components themselves, so no eligible quantity is extracted. No quantity-specific notes are required.
